text:
kevin: Heads-up — seeing a ~12% p99 regression on streaming requests since last runtime change. Suspect batching logic + partial-decode scheduling. Repro: prod/canary, seq_len ~512, model xg-16q.

maria: Thx. I ran a few profiles on canary. pprof shows a spike in kernel selection fallback (int8->fp16) at tail decode, and a lot of small microbatches causing kernel churn.

ashok: Also seeing KV cache churn. Partial decode entries are being evicted when the batch fills and flush cadence shortens; forces rehydration and adds ~3ms/token on tails.

sara: Any config changes recently? Queue weighting? Token caps? :thinking_face: 

kevin: We bumped token_budget_target from 256 -> 384 in the throughput tuning PR. It now waits longer to reach budget which increases batch formation time on streaming edges.

maria: Quick flame from pprof (top):
```
edge_wait_loop: 40%\nkernel_select: 20%\nkv_rehydrate: 12%\ncuda_memcpy: 10%\n```
Notably kernel_select is oscillating between two kernels.

ashok: Proposed quick experiment A/B: revert token_budget_target to 256, lower batch_window_ms to 8ms, and enable prefer_early_flush_for_streaming=true.

sara: I would also tweak queue policy: boost partial-decode queue weight when streaming flag is set (e.g., 1.5x) so short streamed tails don't get starved by big chat batches.

kevin: OK. I'll push a canary with these settings: 
```
"batching": {"token_budget_target":256, "batch_window_ms":8, "prefer_early_flush_for_streaming":true},\n"queue_weights": {"partial_decode":1.5, "standard":1.0}
```

ci-bot: deploy/canary started by kevin — run_id=ci-20260317-42

maria: After 30m: p99 down ~9%, avg latency ~same, throughput -2.5%. KV misses on streaming tails down ~6%.

ashok: kernel_change_count/request dropped ~30% — fewer kernel fallbacks. That matches the decreased kernel_select oscillation.

kevin: Nice. Next idea: kernel-aware batcher that groups incoming requests by kernel_hint (dtype + seq_len bucket) so we avoid mid-batch kernel handoffs. Tag requests at enqueue time.

sara: Caution: grouping by kernel_hint can increase head-of-line blocking for long chats. We need a hybrid: prefer grouping but with a max_hold_ms so we don't block.

maria: Also add two metrics for observability: kernel_group_wait_ms and kv_eviction_rate per request_id. We'll need them to see tradeoffs.

kevin: Agreed. I'll implement kernel_hint tag + max_hold_ms=6ms and add the metrics. Running an overnight job.

ashok: One more tweak for partial-decode scheduling: when streaming=true, schedule the partial decode earlier in the microbatch (i.e., bias slot assignment toward front). That cuts rehydration windows and KV thrash.

kevin: Nice. Implementing that too. Will post results tomorrow. Thanks all :rocket:
